assertions.source: |c5/c4| > 1 in only 1/12, range 0.7077..1.3036, straddling 1; the exceedance is the canonical ordering

assertions.name: A5_scope_of_what_survives_is_stated

assertions.name: A6_sample_supports_falsification_only
assertions.source: 11 counterexamples to the convergence claim; no distributional claim made

description: Tests the two claims qou-441t made from a single bond ordering at A=5, over twelve orderings (canonical production plus eleven random shuffles of the ten bonds). They come apart. THE SIGN IS ROBUST: c5 > 0 in 12 of 12, over the range +1.60 to +3.26, with the identical sign pattern + - - + in every ordering — so the correction to qou-bc09 and qou-38i9 stands, and 'every many-body term is negative' is false from A=5 regardless of convention. THE CONVERGENCE CLAIM IS NOT: |c5/c4| > 1 in only 1 of 12, and that one is the canonical production ordering, the only one qou-441t tested. The ratio ranges 0.7077..1.3036 and straddles 1, so 'the hierarchy does not converge' was an artifact of its convention and is WITHDRAWN; whether the hierarchy converges is unknown. The reason the two behave differently is visible in the spreads: c2 is exactly ordering-independent (a two-element subset has one bond and no internal order), while c3 swings over -2.40..-3.79, c4 over -1.23..-4.19 and c5 over +1.60..+3.26, each by a factor 1.6 to 3.4, with their sum moving less — the ordering artifact redistributes weight between orders. A sign survives that; a ratio between two swinging quantities does not, which applies to anything else in this arc quoted as a cumulant ratio at fixed convention. Untouched: qou-441t's cumulant IDENTIFICATION, that L is additive on disjoint blocks so the Mobius inversion is a genuine cumulant expansion — an exact algebraic fact no ordering affects.
caveats: WITHDRAWS A CLAIM OF MINE FROM THE PREVIOUS TURN. qou-441t's 'the hierarchy does not converge' rested on the canonical ordering alone and does not survive eleven others. Its sign result and its cumulant identification both do. Anyone quoting qou-441t should quote this alongside it.

TWELVE ORDERINGS IS ENOUGH TO FALSIFY, NOT TO CHARACTERISE. One counterexample refutes a universal claim and there are eleven; but no distribution is estimated and none should be read in. 'c5 > 0 in 12/12' is reported as a count, not as a probability, and a thirteenth ordering could in principle differ.

ONE NUCLEON ORDERING ONLY. All twelve trials use 5He at production nucleon ordering 'pnpnn' and vary only the BOND order. Nucleon ordering is a separate artifact (measured at 4-5% in three_body_term_has_the_wrong_sign_probe) and is not varied here.
